articles.title: Lift Out of Service at Derker Tram Stop
articles.excerpt: The lift at Derker tram stop is currently out of service, impacting step-free access for passengers. Alternative routes are available for those travelling towards and away from Manchester.
articles.content_html:
The lift at Derker tram stop is out of service as of 19 August 2026, affecting access for passengers. The disruption is expected to last until further notice, according to the latest travel alerts from the Bee Network.

For customers travelling towards Manchester, step-free access is available via a ramp from Cromford Street directly to the Manchester-bound platform. Those travelling away from Manchester can also use a ramp from Cromford Street, followed by a track crossing to reach the Rochdale-bound platform.

The Bee Network has apologised for any inconvenience caused by this disruption and encourages passengers to plan their journeys accordingly. Passengers are advised to check the Bee Network's travel alerts for the latest information on the lift's status and any other service changes that may affect their travel.

Further details can be found on the Bee Network's official website.

articles.title: Heywood's Pride in Place Scheme Seeks New Chair Following Brian Davies' Resignation
articles.excerpt: The Pride in Place scheme in Heywood is currently without a chair after Brian Davies stepped down, prompting a search for new leadership to guide the £20 million initiative into its delivery phase.
articles.content_html:
The Pride in Place scheme in Heywood is temporarily without a chair following the resignation of Brian Davies. This £20 million initiative, aimed at transforming the town, is now seeking new leadership to guide it through its next phase.

Elsie Blundell, MP for Heywood and Middleton North, praised Davies for his efforts in securing government approval for the investment plan and initiating the scheme. She expressed excitement about the upcoming transition to the delivery phase, stating that the community's priorities include addressing crime and anti-social behaviour, improving transport links, and enhancing facilities for young people.

The Pride in Place project is community-led, with board members representing various local stakeholders, including residents, community organisations, and businesses. The scheme has secured funding of £2 million per year for ten years, and the board is now focused on developing and implementing projects that will shape the future of Heywood.

The search for a new chair and two additional board members is underway, with Blundell encouraging interested individuals to contact her office for more information. The deadline for applications is 7th September, and the new leadership will play a crucial role in engaging with key stakeholders and ensuring the successful delivery of the project.

articles.title: Rochdale Valiant Launches New Media Portal for Community News
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Valiant has introduced a new media portal aimed at providing timely news and information for local residents, enhancing community engagement.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Valiant has launched a new media portal designed to serve as a contemporary news and information source for the community. The initiative, which promotes 'On Point Articulation', focuses on public protection through published media.

The portal aims to engage local residents with timely updates and relevant news, reflecting the needs of a 21st-century audience. It is part of a broader effort to enhance communication within the Rochdale area.

This new platform is expected to facilitate better access to information and encourage community involvement in local affairs. It aims to be a reliable source for news and updates that matter to residents.

For more information, residents can visit the Rochdale Valiant website at Rochdale Valiant.
